correctness.rationale: Derivation is a direct exactly checked 4-variable Hermite Jacobian. For positive secants its signs are (-,+,+,-) and sum to 1. Harmonic derivative upper limits make its one-norm exactly bounded by 1+2t(1-t)(q(a,b)(1-t)+q(c,b)t); arbitrarily small positive outer secants and a sign-matched monotone-preserving perturbation attain the supremum as a limit. Integrating gradients through the convex monotone cone proves global Lipschitz sharpness. A one-variable derivative proves the unique maximum; strict convexity of q(a,b) in a gives the unique balanced minimizer. Rational finite checks passed but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The nontrivial mathematical gap concerns worst-case sensitivity of a nonlinear range-preserving interpolation to changes between two monotone data vectors. The exact local condition number shows unbounded sensitivity on collapsing neighboring spacings despite individual range preservation, and identifies a unique minimax local mesh balancing rule under a natural fixed neighboring-cell budget; applications include noise-sensitive shape-preserving multilevel interpolation. It is not a rephrasing of routine monotonicity or a tiny unmotivated numerical threshold.
